data.narrative:
Mainspring Energy is a Series F climate and energy technology company founded by Shannon Miller, Adam Simpson, and Matt Svrcek that has raised $650M+ to date. The valuation landscape for frontier energy comprises one public comparable (ticker LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method was the applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $650M as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical for Series F progression yields an implied valuation of $845M. This method reflects the capital intensity and typical return expectations at the Series F stage but does not incorporate peer benchmarking. A peer-median approach was not viable; while eight same-sector peers exist, none qualified as same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables, falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $718M to $972M, centered on $845M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty, particularly around the appropriate step-up multiplier for this capital-intensive sector and the lack of direct peer validation. Material sensitivities include technology maturation risk, capital requirements to commercialization, and commodity price exposure. A fuller valuation would benefit from direct comparable transaction data or a broader peer set with transparent valuation and revenue metrics.
